Comments: On 7/26/2024 the dept Oil and Gas inspectors Cody Murray and Geoffrey Lutty conducted an onsite inspection of the Joseph R Spinner 187C permit# 021-20859 There is no visible well posting and no well tag ID on the well anywhere other than faded paint marker on the side of the well head. The 2023 annual production and mechanical assessment reports have not been submitted. Violations will be issues. As the well has not been in production for over a year, it is defined as abandoned. The operator must plug or produce the well. Violations will be issued. properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 3/09/2026 to OIL & GAS MGMT INC in Allegheny Township, Westmoreland county. 102.22(a) - SITE STABILIZATION – PERMANENT STABILIZATION – Permitee failed to have site permanently stabilized and protected from accelerated erosion and sedimentation upon final completion of earth disturbance activity.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: OIL & GAS MGMT INC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 3/09/2026
Violation Code: 102.22(a) - SITE STABILIZATION – PERMANENT STABILIZATION – Permitee failed to have site permanently stabilized and protected from accelerated erosion and sedimentation upon final completion of earth disturbance activity.
Violation ID: 8267362
Permit API: 129-24171
Unconventional: No
County: Westmoreland
Municipality: Allegheny Township
Inspection Type: Follow-up Inspection
Inspection Date: 3/09/2026
Comments: On March 9, 2026, the Department conducted a Follow Up Inspection of Oil and Gas Mgmt's Armstrong 2 well located in Allegheny Township, Westmoreland County following Complaint Inspection 3891447 where violations were issued for inadequate stabilization of the direct and shared portions of the access road that leads to the Armstrong 2 site. A notice of violation (NOV) operator response has yet to be received from the Operator of this Oil and Gas well following IR 3891447, however, a NOV response was received for a nearby well site operated by a separate Operator that received the same violations for the shared portion of the Armstrong 2's access road, and that NOV response stated that repairs to the shared portion of the road would be conducted in the Spring of 2025.At the time of this inspection, the Department observed the condition of the shared portion of Wildcat Road to be worse than what was observed during the Department's last inspection (IR 3990630), major rutting, mud puddles and erosion rills were observed throughout. Wildcat Road eventually leads to a fork, left leading to another well site (the JC Armstrong Jr 1), and right leading directly to the Armstrong 2 well site. Along the direct portions of the Armstrong 2 well site, the Department observed large areas of the access road to be flooded. An exposed pipe was observed alongside the access road, however no methane or other odor was detected, the exposed portion of the pipe did not appear to be compromised. The Department is requesting within 14 days of the receipt of this inspection report, Oil and Gas Management coordinate with the Operator that also utilizes the shared portions of the access road and provide the Department with a written timeline of access road remedial actions for both the shared and direct portions of the access road.At the time of this inspection, the Department observed the Armstrong 2 well site to be overgrown with vegetation, the Department recommends the Operator maintain the vegetation within the well site to ensure the well site remains accessible. A well tag was observed to be fixed to a heavily rusted gas well with all required information posted on it and no fluid leaks or fluid discharges were observed coming from or near the surface of the gas well at this time. A heavily rusted production tank was also observed on site, no fluid leaks or fluid discharges were observed coming from or near this tank at this time. The Department recommends the Operator monitor and maintain the structural integrity of the production tank to ensure the corrosion does not worsen resulting in a release. Violations are being issued in a separate inspection report for the heavily rusted production equipment due to their corrosion posing the risk of a spill and/or release.Based on today's inspection, violations issued for an inadequately stabilized access road is to remain outstanding at this time.

properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 5/06/2025 to DIVERSIFIED PROD LLC in Susquehanna Township, Cambria county. 91.34(A) - ACTIVITIES UTILIZING POLLUTANTS - Failure to take necessary measures to prevent the substances from directly or indirectly reaching waters of this Commonwealth, through accident, carelessness, maliciousness, hazards of weather or from another cause.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: DIVERSIFIED PROD LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 5/06/2025
Violation Code: 91.34(A) - ACTIVITIES UTILIZING POLLUTANTS - Failure to take necessary measures to prevent the substances from directly or indirectly reaching waters of this Commonwealth, through accident, carelessness, maliciousness, hazards of weather or from another cause.
Violation ID: 8232620
Permit API: 021-21034
Unconventional: No
County: Cambria
Municipality: Susquehanna Township
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 5/06/2025
Comments: On May 6, 2025, an inspection was conducted in response to a spill at the A J Stahura 8 well site in Susquehanna Township, Cambria County. This spill was discovered by the operator on the day prior to this inspection, which is suspected by the operator to have been caused by trespassing vandals opening the brine tank valve when operator representatives were not present onsite. The Department spoke with operator representative Will Warfel on 5/05/2025, who stated that the last time operator representatives were onsite was most likely one month prior to detecting this spill, when the chart was changed and the brine tank level was read. Reporting of this spill is covered in IR 3974873. Mr. Warfel was onsite was onsite with the Department during this inspection.The following was observed:Upon arrival, the Department spoke with Mr. Warfel who identified a stream crossing of Kings Run as part of the access road to the well site (see photo 1). He then requested recommendations for dispersing the weight of commercial vehicles that haul the excavation equipment onsite to protect the cross-culverts when they traverse this location (see photo 4). Further review will be conducted by the Department regarding this matter. What appears to be scouring was observed on the upstream side of the stream crossing. A brown foam that appears to be biological in nature was observed at the top of the water in this location (see photo 3). An erosion channel was going down the access road toward the downstream location of the stream crossing (see photos 5 and 6). Mr. Warfel stated that this access road is utilized by additional parties. Further review via Google Earth Historic Imagery suggests that this portion of the access road most likely predates the well site. Additional muddy tire rutting was observed in the rest of the access road going toward the well site (see photos 7 and 8).The well head is equipped with a well tag and appears to be free of fluid leaks at the time of inspection (see photo 10). The operator's information is posted on the brine tank (see photo 11). The body of the brine tank appears to be sound at the time of inspection (see photos 12 and 14). The brine tank valve appears to have been closed, therefore it appears that the release has been ceased (see photo 13). Plastic sheeting was placed on the impacted area within the earthen berm. Distressed vegetation was observed where brine fluids were reported by the operator to have traveled downslope (see photos 15-17). Elevated conductivity was detected in the ground starting approximately 25 feet downslope of the brine tank (see photos 18-25). Mr. Warfel confirmed during this inspection that the operator will conduct remediation in accordance with the requirements of Act 2, and that remediation will start on the day of this inspection with light excavation.Based on observations from this inspection, violations shall be issued from this inspection for releasing production fluids to the surface of the ground. The operator is requested to submit a written response within 15 business days of the spill or release. This response should include an incident report, a timeline, the regulation substance involved, where the spill or release occur, the environmental media affected, any impacts to water supplies, buildings, or utilities, and interim actions planned, initiated, or completed.Any new impacts discovered or identified during interim remedial actions or site characterization should also be reported to the Department within 15 calendar days of discovery.Within 180 days of the spill or release the operator must perform a site characterization to determine the extent and magnitude of the contamination and submit the site characterization report to the undersigned.The operator shall assess impacts to waters of the Commonwealth from the spill or release.

Report Details

Violation Code: 78.54 - GENERAL REQUIREMENTS - Operator failed to control and dispose of fluids, residual waste and drill cuttings, including tophole water, brines, drilling fluids, drilling muds, stimulation fluids, well servicing fluids, oil, and production fluids in a manner that prevents pollution of the waters of the Commonwealth.

Permit API: 129-27774
Unconventional: No
County: Westmoreland
Municipality: Manor Boro
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 2/03/2023
Comments: On February 3 2023, the Department conducted an inspection in response to a spill release reported by the Operator on 2/2/2023 for the Cummins 1 OG Well. Accompanying in today's inspection was Ron Truitt (Penneco Represenative). The findings were as follows:Per Ron Truitt, produced water was released due to the overflowing of the right production tank. The nipple (where the two tanks connect)at the top of the production tank was frozen and did not allow back flow from one tank to another. The back flow not being able to flow from one tank to another caused the right tank to overflow. Per Ron Truitt, it was estimated that approximately 1 barrel of produced water was released. The Department recommends that the Operator remediate the affected area in accordance with the spill policy for releases greater than 42 gallons.At the time of the inspection, clean up was being conducted. The production tanks were being emptied. Impacted area was being excavated. The Department requests that the Operator submit waste manifests once available. The Department will conduct a follow up inspection to verify that all impacted material has been removed. Based on today's inspection violations are being issued.

Code § 78a.52a (c) to the Department at least 30 days prior to commencement of drilling the well or at the time the permit application was submitted when the operator planned to commence drilling the well less than 30 days from the date of permit issuance.
Violation ID: 8262766
Permit API: 117-22313
Unconventional: Yes
County: Tioga
Municipality: Middlebury Township
Inspection Type: Administrative/File Review
Inspection Date: 1/28/2026
Comments: On 12/18/2025, the Department issued a total of four (4) new drilling permits to Seneca Resources for unconventional gas wells located on the Chappell D 855 pad in Middlebury Township, Tioga County. Review of Department records indicates that the Chappell 855 169HU (API #37-117-22313) was spud on 1/6/2026 and the Area of Review (AOR) report was submitted to the Department on 1/14/2026. This represents a violation of ¿¿78a.52a(d), which states: "The operator shall submit the report required under subsection (c) to the Department at least 30 days prior to the start of drilling the well or at the time the permit application is submitted if the operator plans to start drilling the well less than 30 days from the date of permit issuance." Although the AOR report was not submitted at least 30 days prior to spudding or with the drilling permit application for the Chappell 855 169HU as required, the AOR report was ultimately submitted to the Department so a Violation Immediately Corrected (VIOIC) has been cited for this gas well. It should be noted that the same issue occurred at the other three (3) gas wells that were recently permitted at the Chappell D 855 pad. Moving forward, Seneca Resources should take all measures necessary to submit AOR reports in a manner that complies with the regulation referenced above.

Inspection Date: 4/05/2023
Comments: I received a text message on April 3rd 2023 from the OGI that was checking on the flaring operation being conducted on the Hill Lease in Brokenstraw twp Warren county operated by Universal Resource Holdings. He said there was a oil spill that appears to have taken place awhile ago coming from a well close to the one being flared. On 04/04/2023, I followed up on the information, Brad Hofert from Universal resource holding was onsite at the time of my inspection. Brad said a valve had frozen and blew out on the number 21 well over winter. The valve was replaced and absorbent pads were used to clean up around the wellhead. I returned to the site on 04/05/2023 to gather photos and take another look at the extent of the spill.Evidence of the crude made it down slope approx 150 feet but stayed inside the tire ruts. More than likely carried by snow melt and rain. Oil soaked leaves and some oxidized crude can be seen in the tire ruts. The estimated release amount is around 5 gallons of crude. I spoke with Brad about getting the oil soaked leaf litter cleaned up and some of the soil next to the well head removed. He agreed and said he would get a crew together and a mini excavator to scrape up the area near the well head. With the estimated volume of this release and the small affected area, this is a non reportable release. The oil covered leaf litter and impacted soil will need to be properly disposed of.

Comments: Site inspection conducted to review drill cuttings processing activity and secondary containment conditions at the Taft 851 well pad. Meeting on site with Seneca Company Man Carlos Martinez. Weather conditions are mostly sunny and 65F.According to Mr. Martinez, the Patterson 805 rig is tripping drill pipe back into the well following a tool change. The rig is working on the tangent section of the 71HU well (API# 117-22261). The rig will resume drilling at a depth of 8,786' and work to a Total Depth of 24,073'. Drilling will resume around 1600 hours. This is the fourth well of eight total to be drilled in this setup. There are five wells in production at this well pad. Solids control in the rig backyard is managed by White's Energy Services. Shakers and centrifuges are idle at time of inspection. Steel bins are mostly empty of drill cuttings. The rig mats in the backyard are clean and free of debris (photos 3-6). Seneca submitted a Request for Approval of Alternate Waste Management Practices (OG-71) Form A application for the Taft Pad on 4/25/25. The Department approved the request on 5/1/25. The request for the approval of Alternative Waste Management Practices is for drill cuttings processing and solids removal from drilling mud. See photos and comments in the on-site processing findings section of this inspection report below, and refer to the Taft OG-71 Form A application, eFACTS Authorization ID#1525611.During this inspection, water along the north pad ditch line was screened for elevated conductivity using an Oakton PCTS50 meter. Water with electrical conductivity (4.02 mS/cm) is observed in the ditch line between the pad rock and the berm along the north side of the well pad (photo 12). Water within the sediment basin was screened and found to have elevated conductivity reading of 2.29 mS/cm. Violations remain outstanding against permit #117-22231 for pollutional water found on site and documented in Inspection Reports #3736567 and #3724668.The Department requests Seneca submit copies of weekly containment inspection and repair logs for the dates August 4-August 25, to juabbott@pa.gov.

Unconventional: No

Inspection Date: 3/18/2021
Comments: On 3/18/21 at 1153 hrs., I conducted an inspection of DiversifiedProduction, LLC's F Kinter 3 well (API 063-35436) in Center Twp., Indiana Co. in response to a reported release of 42.5 barrels of production fluid onto the ground from a tank located onsite. According to the operator, corroded threads on a coupling connected to the tank was the cause of the release. Photos were submitted to the Department prior to inspection of the site. The release impacted the earthen berm containment area and a portion of an agricultural field to the north of the berm. Conductivity readings were elevated both within the earthen berm and outside the berm, indicating migration through the berm and soil in the adjacent field. The operator had tentatively delineated the northern extent of the migration with yellow flags. Soil conductivity beyond the northern most flag was at background level. The operator notified the Department that remediation of the site would commence on Monday, 3/22/21. The release of production fluids from a tank onto the ground constitutes violations of SWMA 301, SWMA 302(A), SWMA 610(1), and 78.57(a). The violations associated with this release will be resolved upon remediation of the site and attainment of an Act 2 standard. Please refer to Page 3 of this Notice of Violation regarding a written response describing how you intend to remediate the release and demonstrate attainment of an Act 2 standard.

properties.summary: Administrative violation issued on 7/24/2023 to ALLSHOUSE TERRENCE L JR in Pleasant Township, Warren county. OGA3211(H) - WELL PERMITS - LABELING - Failure to install, in a permanent manner, the permit number on a completed well.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: ALLSHOUSE TERRENCE L JR
Violation Type: Administrative
Violation Date: 7/24/2023
Violation Code: OGA3211(H) - WELL PERMITS - LABELING - Failure to install, in a permanent manner, the permit number on a completed well.
Violation ID: 8153665
Permit API: 123-42130
Unconventional: No
County: Warren
Municipality: Pleasant Township
Inspection Type: Complaint Inspection
Inspection Date: 7/24/2023
Comments: This well was inspected as part of an on going stray gas migration case involving gas migrating into a private water supply (CTS#373559). The well head and casing strings were observed at the time of inspection for leaks, deterioration, corrosion, and possible failures. As part of the investigation 3 slam bar holes were placed into the ground approximately 1-2 feet from the well head to identify if any methane was migrating from the well-bore. All valves were open and the well is currently equipped for production. 2 check valves were in place on the production lines and were oriented correctly. Well records, production reports, and mechanical integrity assessment reports were reviewed to assist in the investigation. NO methane was detected in the slam bar holes utilizing a MSA ALTAIR 5X meter which was calibrated on 07/17/2023. No casing string pressures were observed at the time of inspection due to no pressure gauges in place and no operator provided well tender available. This well was labeled with an incorrect well API#, this issue was brought to the attention of the operator and promptly fixed. Further inspections of this well may be warranted to determine the root cause of the complaint.

Violation ID: 8179688
Permit API: 125-22817
Unconventional: No
County: Washington
Municipality: Fallowfield Township
Inspection Type: Follow-up Inspection
Inspection Date: 3/11/2024
Comments: On 03/11/2024, a follow up inspection was conducted at the Molek F19 well site following violations issued on 12/08/2023 (IR 3657799, Enforcement 419234). I was accompanied by Environmental Trainees Olivia Holley, Madison Raviart, and Christina Mauri (PA DEP).On 12/08/2023, violations of 102.11(a), 102.22(a)2ii, and 78.53 were issued as outstanding for the access road. Inspection from 12/28/2023 noted that the violations were still open, however the operator was in compliance with schedule. On 01/24/2024, the violations were outstanding (IR 3701625). The following was observed:Some stabilization was used along the upper portion of the access road. Several areas throughout the entire access road did not have stabilization on the open soils. I recommend that stabilization is applied (Photos 1-4). Some areas had vegetation establishing (Photos 2, 4, 5).The channel that runs along the access road did not have rip rap or stabilization. Accelerated erosion and sediment accumulation were noted within this channel, which leads to several culverts along the road (Photo 6).The upper culvert, located at 40.113707 -79.966213, had sediment accumulation within the collection point. I recommend that this is addressed (Photo 7). The culvert located at 40.11300, -79.96751 had large amounts of sediment accumulated within the collection point. The culvert was not able to be seen due to the large amount of sediment within this area (Photos 8, 9). Accelerated erosion was noted within the accumulated sediment (Photo 9). The outlet point of this culvert was covered by the roads gravel/dirt, which was causing accelerated erosion and sediment transport towards the vegetation (Photos 10-12). I recommend that this is addressed. The culvert leading to the collection box was not functioning. Sediment was accumulated and an entry point into the pipe was approximately 99% covered. Accelerated erosion and sedimentation throughout the area and vegetation were noted leading from the channel towards the collection box. There was some sediment laden water within this box. This outlets into the vegetation, where sediment accumulation was noted. The vegetation was accumulating water, which leads towards the stream within the wood line (Photos 13-19). The lower culvert outlets into a channel. Sediment accumulation was noted within the channel. I recommend that rip rap is used within this channel, as this leads directly to the stream (Photos 20, 21).The culverts along the first portion of the access road, near the site gate, were not cleaned out. Potholes along the road were not addressed. Channelization was noted leading from the potholes off of the road. The beginning of the access road, where it meets the township road, was not addressed. This area was previously displaying high levels of flow, leading onto the township road, and depositing sediment. This was noted within IR 3701625, photos 24 and 15 (Photos 22-25). The violations issued on 01/24/2024, IR 3701625, remain outstanding.

Unconventional: Yes
County: Bradford
Municipality: Albany Township
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 1/27/2025
Comments: Incident Inspection of Expand's "Dunham" Marcellus well site.Expand is using this Marcellus well pad to stage equipment for hydraulically fracturing Marcellus wells at their nearby "Henry" site. Steve Moyer (Expand) called the DEP on Saturday January 18, 2025 to report an estimated 45-50 gallon release of produced liquid from an unknown source to the pad surface they discovered that day at 1445 hrs. Creston Environmental delineated the impacted area of the pad surface at approximately 35'x35' using electrical conductivity (EC) meters. They excavated to remove impacted pad material the day after its discovery. Creston sampled the pad material in accordance to Act 2 cleanup.Vegetation and rock stabilize soil of the site, but cannot fully assess stabilization because of partial snow cover. I did not see accelerated erosion or sedimentation on site. Post Construction Stormwater Management (PCSM) controls are in place and appear to be functioning as designed. Containment structures are intact. I did not observe any leaks or other deficiencies.Both Marcellus well cellars are full of snow/ice.I did not see any pooled water on the pad surface, just snow/ice. I could not get electrical conductivity readings with a Hanna Soil Test probe because the pad material is frozen solid. Air temp 27FJLP

Violation ID: 978530
Permit API: 053-30164
Unconventional: Yes
County: Forest
Municipality: Hickory Twp
Inspection Type: Follow-up Inspection
Inspection Date: 12/12/2022
Comments: On 12/12/2022, I conducted a follow up inspection of the DR02 Pad and Impoundment ESX 1H well. Nucomer has hired a 3rd party contractor "Assist" to complete the secondary containment liner repair. TJ Pennino from EMKEY Gathering was on site representing Nucomer Energy. This is in response to violations in previous inspections(3459581). The violations are for tears and holes in the secondary containment liner in the tank battery. Two different methods were being utilized in the repair attempt. One is a hot air weld of liner material. The second was a PVC extruder gun as seen in photo #3. It should be noted the original containment liner is thickness of 20 mil. The patch material brought by Assist for the hot air welding is a 40 mil thickness. After several attempts to hot air weld the patch material to the existing liner, it was evident trying to weld the 40 mil patch material to the 20 mil existing material was not going to work. Several pieces of the 20 mil liner were cut from outside containment and cleaned as best as possible. Again the original liner material is too thin and was not supporting a good hot-air weld. The extruder was used on several smaller holes. It became obvious it is not suitable to be used on a material of this thickness. The temperature was set as low as the machine would allow and the material melted through the original liner (pictures #1 and #4).After several attempts trying several different methods, the decision was made by TJ to abandon the repair attempt. TJ was going to speak with ASSIST and plan another course of action and discuss options available.Additionally the violation for the 55 gallon drums being stored outside of secondary containment, can be closed. This violation has been resolved.

Comments: On 02/26/2025 Expand representative Steven Moyer reported a discovered release onsite. He stated "there was a hole in containment. They picked up the containment around 1100 hours that morning. An unknown amount of frack water mixed with stormwater on pad. Creston Environmental will be conducting the cleanup." On 02/27/2026 the Department of Environmental Protection (DEP) conducted an incident response inspection of the Wygrala Well Pad in Wysox Township, Bradford County. The weather was 30 degrees and sunny. I arrived at 0915 hours. Upon arrival to the site DEP met with Expand representative Danielle Schadd and two Creston Environmental representatives. The area of the reported release is estimated to be an area of 75x150. There were barricades in place to keep the area closed off to vehicles (photo #2). Within the 75x150 area the elevated conductivity of the soil varies between 0-4 mS/cm. There were no pooled fluids within the reported release area. Approximately 2-3 inches of material had already been excavated and placed into containment onsite. Alderdice, Inc. was onsite removing the material during the inspection. Creston Environmental was conducting further testing during the inspection. They were going to expand their testing area due to the ground thawing with increased temperatures. The cause of the release was due to a ripped seam in the pad wide containment. This caused freshwater and brine mixture to leak through onto the pad surface. The same pad wide containment was in place during stimulation (01/23/2026-02/12/2926) and drill out (02/15/2026-02/18/2026). The quantity of the release is unknown. Due to the unknown quantity of the release this is being referred to ECB for Act 2 compliance.Based on the reported release (CTS #395411) the following violations have been cited against API #015-23981:CSL 402(b)35 P.S. 6018.301 SWMA25 Pa. Code 78a.56(a)I departed at 1000 hours.

A violation was issued in IR 4170358 for failure to remove equipment that is not necessary for production, in accordance with in accordance with OGA3216(C). The well site overall exhibits greater than 70% uniform and adequate vegetative growth. No accelerated erosion and sedimentation concerns are observed at this time (photos 5 and 12).Based on observations from this inspection, violations that were continued in IR 4168852 shall remain outstanding, as it appears that no corrective action has been taken onsite since the date of that inspection and no response of any kind to IR 3093059 has been received to date.

Comments: On November 2, 2023, DEP representative Brad Kline conducted an incident inspection at the Range Resources Laurel Hill Pad D. Kirby Steck from Range Resources reported a spill of approximately 3.5 barrels of production fluid. The spill occurred when a water hauling truck operator forgot to close a valve on the production fluid tanks after removing the production fluid from the tank causing the production fluid to spill on the well pad surface. The production fluid was spilled on the south corner of the well pad at approximate coordinates 41.4837421, -77.1143370. Range Resources contractors onsite immediately began vacuuming the fluid up off the well pad surface. Range Resources delineated the area of impact and contractors began excavating the area of impact. The excavation area was about eighty feet by thirty feet with a depth of about six inches. The impacted soil was placed on containment and Range Resources is awaiting roll off dumpsters to arrive. The excavation of the area had been completed prior to DEP's arrival onsite. properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: APOLLO RESOURCES LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 6/21/2023
Violation Code: 78.104 - INACTIVE STATUS - TERM OF INACTIVE STATUS – After 5 year inactive status term, owner or operator failed to return well to active status, obtain a one year inactive status extension, apply for renewal of inactive status or plug the well.
Violation ID: 1000427
Permit API: 129-24858
Unconventional: No
County: Westmoreland
Municipality: Derry Township
Inspection Type: Follow-up Inspection
Inspection Date: 6/21/2023
Comments: Follow up inspection of the Proffitt 1 well conducted on 6/21/2023. Arrived on location at 09:15. Well is not in, or equipped for, production. Onsite equipment consists of wellhead and pumpjack. Flow lines disconnected at wellhead. Review found Annual Production Reports have been submitted with last production shown in 2016. Well status was previously approved as Regulatory Inactive. Regulatory Inactive status expired on 5/20/2022. Violations were issued on 5/1/2023 for: OGA3211(G) - Well tag had incorrect information. OGA3220(A) - Failure to plug abandoned well. 78.91(a) - Failure to plug abandoned well. 78.103 - Failure to report annual integrity monitoring of the well while under Inactive Status. 78.104 - Failure to meet terms of Inactive Status. 78.88 - Failure to report Mechanical Integrity of the well after expiration of Inactive Status. 78.73(a) - Failure to maintain integrity of the well due to fluid discharging to the ground from the disconnected flow line at the wellhead. This 6/21/2023 follow up inspection found: OGA3211(G) - Corrected with proper well tag information now in place. 78.73(a) - Corrected with well integrity restored and no longer discharging from flow line at the well head. OGA3220(A) - Remains outstanding due to well being abandoned. 78.91(a) - Remains outstanding due to well being abandoned. 78.103 - Remains outstanding due to no annual integrity reports found. 78.104 - Remains outstanding due to terms of Inactive Status not met. 78.88 - Remains outstanding due to no Mechanical Integrity reports found. Response was received from the operator on 5/30/2023 (attached as file) which indicated the well will be plugged. The Department requests a response to this report with an anticipated timeframe for plugging.
